description: We are a two-person interdisciplinary team combining software, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, electrical-electronics engineering, and telecommunications. Our goal is to transform real space mission concepts and NASA data into an interactive, engaging, and accessible training experience to inspire and prepare future junior astronauts.
summary: Compass Outpost is a browser game for kids ages 7-12 in which the player runs a small Mars research outpost for ten sols with a robot companion, DUTİ. Each sol the player chooses one of three plans, and every plan has a cost: Energy, Oxygen and Safety must stay above zero, and the crew also needs 10 Science points to succeed. A choice that saves power today can cost oxygen tomorrow, and earlier preparations open or close later options. Short hands-on tasks, predictions about the coming night and fact cards turn each trade-off into something the child does and checks. The game is grounded in real NASA data: Perseverance MEDA temperature readings from Jezero Crater, a DONKI coronal mass ejection record with NASA's report on the May 2024 solar storm at Mars, MOXIE oxygen results and real Perseverance and Curiosity photographs, all credited inside the game. It runs in any browser with no download or account, in English with an optional Turkish interface.
details: WHAT IT DOES Compass Outpost: Ten Sols of Questions turns the trade-offs of a Mars outpost into a ten-sol story game for kids ages 7-12. The player is the Commander, and DUTİ, a robot companion, explains each situation in plain language. Each sol offers three plans with visible costs in Energy, Oxygen and Safety. If any resource reaches zero, the research mission stops safely. To succeed after Sol 10 the crew needs at least 1 Energy, 1 Oxygen, 4 Safety and 10 Science. HOW IT WORKS - Every choice has a cost or an opportunity cost. A plan that saves power today can cost oxygen tomorrow. - Nights matter: dust lowers solar charging, and when the battery runs out, life support switches to a low-power mode that uses extra oxygen. - Earlier decisions shape later sols: a rock sample or a greenhouse kept running opens later options, storm-shelter preparation lowers later costs, and the full choice history can unlock one of five special endings. - Hands-on mini tasks (cleaning dusty panels, comparing real temperatures, sending a radio message with a signal delay, sorting clues) make each decision active. - A prediction before selected nights, a morning ledger and fact cards explain why the resources changed. - Three mission profiles (standard, dusty season, small oxygen supply) and the special endings encourage replay and learning from failure without punishment. NASA DATA IN THE GAME - Mars 2020 Perseverance MEDA calibrated air temperatures (NASA Planetary Data System), Sol 290 at Jezero Crater: about -3 °C to -77 °C. Used in the Sol 2 night-power decision and a comparison task. - NASA DONKI record 2024-05-20T05:36:00-CME-001 and NASA's report on the May 2024 solar storm observed at Mars (about 8,100 micrograys for an astronaut beside Curiosity). Used in the Sol 5 radiation-protection decision. - NASA results on MOXIE oxygen production, Perseverance sample tubes, Veggie plant growth, Mars facts and Earth-Mars signal delay, shown in fact cards and discoveries. - Three NASA photographs: PIA19400, PIA24765 and PIA26373. The data is archived and embedded in the game, labelled "archival data, not live", and every source is linked inside the game. Resource points and fictional events are game values and are labelled as such. The visitor ending is clearly marked as science fiction. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Children experience why mission planners must balance power, life support and protection, instead of only reading facts about Mars. The game needs no download or account, works on phones and computers, supports mouse, touch and keyboard, and has an optional Turkish interface. TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules, no build step), SVG illustrations drawn in code, Web Audio for synthesized sound, Anime.js, canvas-confetti and the Fredoka typeface. A pure rules engine is checked path by path against an independent reference model with Node.js scripts, and Playwright browser tests cover input, layout, language switching and saving. AI tools assisted development as disclosed in AI_USAGE.md and ai-usage.json in the repository. LIMITS The game has not yet been playtested with children of the target age, so no measured learning outcome is claimed.
